newsitem.title: UK: Deng has left repression machine in place - Amnesty.
newsitem.headline: Deng has left repression machine in place - Amnesty.

text.p: Amnesty International said on Wednesday night that the death of Chinese leader Deng Xiaoping had left in place a "well-oiled machinery for repression", and it urged China to keep up its law reforms.
"The transition from Deng Xiaoping will be a testing time for the future course of human rights in China," the human rights group said in a statement.
Beijing announced earlier on Wednesday that Deng, the 93-year-old paramount leader, had died of complications from Parkinson's disease and a lung infection. He had ruled China since 1978.
Repression against organised dissent had already increased in the past year because Chinese authorities feared instability in the period after Deng's death, Amnesty said.

"Deng will be remembered for beginning the overhaul of China's economic system and consequent legal reform. But his legacy also includes a well-oiled machinery for repression, where the law is used as a weapon against dissent."
Amnesty "urged the Chinese leadership to maintain the momentum of law reform."

Uncertainty about the future was especially great in Hong Kong which Britain is to hand over to Chinese rule later this year, Rory Mungoven, director of Amnesty's Asia-Pacific programme, said. "It is vitally important that the autonomy and safeguards for human rights which were built into Hong Kong's transition plan under Deng's oversight remain in place," Mungoven said.
